inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,457 Python-split logical lines of the normalized 24-page article. The source develops an exception-aware small-gap mechanism for derivative zeros, proves the CUE near-boundary asymptotic through an analytic root expansion and collision-conditioned random-matrix averages, transfers the expansion conjecturally to zeta zeros under CUE statistics, derives the needed one-level density by orthogonal-polynomial kernels, and supplies an argument-principle proof of uniqueness and analyticity. Formula extraction is mostly recoverable from prose and equation labels, with isolated control-character splits in displayed formulas and detached plot coordinates.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the zeta/CUE comparison, the proved leading CUE asymptotic, and the unexplained bimodal observation.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects derivative-zero location to RH and sets the mean-spacing-normalized random-matrix bridge.

sections_inspected.label: 2. The zeros of zeta prime
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the Levinson-method loss, local gap evidence, derivative-zero density mismatch, and Soundararajan distributional criteria.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Polynomial derivatives and results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the unit-circle polynomial analogue, defines scaled radial distance, states the small-gap theorem and full-density corollary, and records their limits.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Comparison with data
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reports numerical agreement and bimodality across CUE, COE, Poisson, and zeta settings.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Proof of Theorem 3.1, including interleaved Section 4 figures
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the analytic close-pair root expansion, pushes spacing statistics through it, conditions the ensemble on a collision, and evaluates the needed coefficient averages.

sections_inspected.label: 6. The Riemann zeta-function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Repeats the local logarithmic-derivative expansion for zeta and identifies the CUE-dependent coefficient match and numerical comparison.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Calculation of the 1-level density
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the collision-weighted limiting density through OPUC projection kernels and Jacobi-to-Bessel asymptotics.

sections_inspected.label: 8. Appendix: domain of analyticity
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves existence, uniqueness, and analytic dependence of the derivative root in the close-pair disk by an argument-principle perturbation estimate.

sections_inspected.label: References and author back matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic provenance and affiliations; no further source-developed mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Derivative-zero exclusion as an RH criterion
accepted_units.why_material: The source makes derivative zeros a structural diagnostic: RH is equivalent to excluding zeros of zeta prime left of the critical line, while a quantitative refinement localizes a positive proportion near that line.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the distinction between Speiser's equivalence and the later quantitative localization; the latter is motivation, not itself an RH equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The equivalence is explicit in prose; the localization bound depends on the displayed formula at lines 35-37, which is readable despite degraded one-half typography.

accepted_units.title: Horizontal zeta-prime distance versus radial characteristic-polynomial distance
accepted_units.why_material: This is the paper's central representation change: local zeta statistics at height T are modeled by CUE characteristic polynomials with N approximately log(T/2pi), turning horizontal derivative-zero location into radial derivative-root location.
accepted_units.context_note: The bridge is explicitly conditional on random-matrix modeling and combines prior evidence, this paper's CUE theorem, an analogous zeta calculation, and numerical comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Recoverable from prose; exact normalization uses inline formulas whose primes and pi symbols should be retained from the source.

accepted_units.title: Near-critical derivative zeros as an inherent Levinson-method loss
accepted_units.why_material: The passage explains operationally why the horizontal distribution matters: derivative zeros in a thin strip are an unavoidable loss term, and lower bounds there could improve critical-line zero estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a method-level motivation and does not claim that controlling the strip alone proves RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is clear; one-half symbols and the a/log T boundary are formula-layer dependent.

accepted_units.title: Close zeta-zero gaps create nearby derivative zeros, but density forces missing matches
accepted_units.why_material: The example records both sides of the local correspondence: close zeta zeros accompany a derivative zero near the critical line, yet unequal global densities prevent a one-per-gap matching and force missing derivative zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The close-gap statement is presented observationally here and deferred to Section 6 for the asymptotic calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Figure caption and prose are readable; the density formulas are visually fragmented and require scan verification for exact constants.

accepted_units.title: Soundararajan's limiting frequency functions for zeta-prime proximity
accepted_units.why_material: The liminf/limsup functions compress horizontal derivative-zero distribution into a family of testable proximity frequencies, together with continuity, positivity, and mass-at-infinity conjectures and a small-gap conditional result.
accepted_units.context_note: The unconditional and conditional statements must remain separated: the all-a positivity cited at the end assumes a conjecture about small gaps.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions and inequalities rely on multi-line displays with degraded beta-prime and one-half glyphs; use the checked prose for semantics and verify exact notation against the scan before formula reuse.

accepted_units.title: Local root collision controls a derivative root near the unit circle
accepted_units.why_material: Gauss-Lucas, continuity, and locality combine into a reusable mechanism: a close pair of unit-circle roots creates a nearby derivative root whose leading displacement depends on the gap and the background configuration.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage motivates, rather than yet proves, the claim that the small radial tail is governed primarily by nearest-neighbor spacing.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is self-contained; only the final definition of the scaled radial variable depends on a short display.

accepted_units.title: Heavy radial tail reproduces the Levinson-Montgomery scale
accepted_units.why_material: The 1/s-squared radial tail has no finite mean but has a logarithmically growing truncation, which places a positive proportion of derivative roots within log N/N of the circle and matches the zeta scale after density normalization.
accepted_units.context_note: This uses Mezzadri's tail result and the asymptotic density match; it is a random-matrix counterpart, not a proof of the zeta statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual chain is explicit in prose, but the tail, truncated integral, and N-to-T normalization are display-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Translation-invariant CUE spacing and its small-gap expansion
accepted_units.why_material: The source normalizes eigenangles to unit mean spacing, derives index independence from translation invariance, and supplies the small-s nearest-neighbor expansion that later drives the derivative-root density.
accepted_units.context_note: The equality with pair correlation is asserted only through order six, which is exactly the truncation relevant to the later expansion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the CUE joint density and spacing-series displays; coefficients are mostly legible but should be scan-checked for exact downstream computation.

accepted_units.title: Perturb a double root and expand the scaled derivative-root displacement
accepted_units.why_material: A degenerate root anchors an analytically moving derivative root; centering the close pair and expanding its scaled displacement yields the stated small-s density through the s-to-the-three-halves term.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 3.1 covers small derivative-root distances arising from closely spaced polynomial roots, not every small distance.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The perturbative construction is clear in prose; the exact coefficients in equations (3.17)-(3.18) are formula-layer dependent.

accepted_units.title: Small radial derivative distance is not exclusively a close-gap phenomenon
accepted_units.why_material: The source explicitly blocks a tempting converse by citing separated-root families that still produce near-circle derivative roots, then explains why close pairs nevertheless determine the leading square-root density and records the unresolved normalization problem.
accepted_units.context_note: The counterexample contribution vanishes linearly and is lower order than the close-pair square-root term; the full limiting density being proper remains unproved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core distinctions are in prose; the leading asymptotic and total-mass condition depend on readable but degraded displays.

accepted_units.title: Bimodality persists across correlated and independent root ensembles
accepted_units.why_material: Numerics support the asymptotic tail yet expose an unexplained second bump that appears for CUE, COE, independent uniform roots, and zeta-prime data, suggesting a mechanism more general than one ensemble's correlations.
accepted_units.context_note: This is empirical evidence and a question-generating observation, not an explained theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The narrative is readable; quantitative plot shapes reside in figures and would require the retained PDF for precise measurement.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic derivative separates a close pair from its background
accepted_units.why_material: Factoring the polynomial into the close pair and the remaining roots turns the derivative-root equation into a sum of two singular pair terms plus the background logarithmic derivative.
accepted_units.context_note: The rotation placing the midpoint at one and the assumption of no intervening background roots are essential local setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (5.1)-(5.2); extraction preserves the factorization and reciprocal structure well enough for semantic use.

accepted_units.title: Mean-spacing and radial-displacement rescaling for a nontrivial CUE limit
accepted_units.why_material: Rotation invariance reduces the distribution to radial position, and the paired rescalings identify the variables that remain meaningful as matrix size grows.
accepted_units.context_note: The text notes that the angular scaling is immediate while the radial scaling is justified later by cancellation in the implicit equation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Short formula display is readable; surrounding plot material is intentionally excluded.

accepted_units.title: Even analytic root branch and coefficient expansion
accepted_units.why_material: The implicit-function argument, convergence domain, logarithmic-derivative Taylor coefficients, and close-pair expansion combine to show that the scaled displacement is an even analytic function of gap size with explicit first two coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: The background polynomial is held fixed in this derivation; the source postpones justification for the random ensemble to the next subsection.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong dependence on equations (5.4)-(5.16). Prose and labels recover the derivation, but dense extracted fractions and error terms require scan verification before exact symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Push nearest-neighbor spacing through the root map with controlled dependence
accepted_units.why_material: The source converts the complex root displacement to radial distance, pushes the spacing density through the local inverse map, and isolates why the second coefficient may be averaged despite finite-gap dependence.
accepted_units.context_note: The leading radial coefficient is deterministic; approximate independence of the next coefficient is justified only to the needed order by seventh-order vanishing of next-nearest-neighbor spacing.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The mechanism is explicit in prose, while the transformed density and its coefficients are formula-heavy; line 579 is split by an extraction control character.

accepted_units.title: A double eigenvalue induces fourth-power characteristic-polynomial reweighting
accepted_units.why_material: Because exact repeated eigenvalues form a measure-zero event, the source defines collision conditioning by a shrinking-neighborhood limit and shows that expectations of the remaining roots equal Haar expectations reweighted by the fourth power of the characteristic polynomial.
accepted_units.context_note: The limiting construction is the canonical choice for this close-pair problem, not an unconditional restriction of Haar measure to a null set.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose clearly identifies the reweighting; exact measures (5.25)-(5.29) depend on multi-line product displays.

accepted_units.title: Ratio averages reduce random root coefficients to computable expectations
accepted_units.why_material: A generating ratio of characteristic polynomials converts the needed collision-conditioned coefficient moments into derivatives of a known Haar average; computer algebra then supplies the expected second coefficient and closes Theorem 3.1.
accepted_units.context_note: The source does not reproduce the external ratio formula and explicitly reports Mathematica assistance, so this is a computational reduction and reported evaluation rather than a self-contained symbolic derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence. Control characters split several displayed derivatives around lines 750-769; exact identities and coefficients require PDF verification, though the reduction and conclusion are clear.

accepted_units.title: Zeta logarithmic derivative reproduces the CUE close-gap expansion
accepted_units.why_material: Separating two close zeta zeros in the partial-fraction expansion, rescaling by local zero density, and expanding yields the same implicit equation and leading coefficients as the unitary characteristic-polynomial calculation.
accepted_units.context_note: The expected background coefficient and final distributional match assume CUE statistics for zeta zeros; the conclusion is conjectural for zeta, not an RH result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense equations (6.1)-(6.17) are essential and some fractions are visually fragmented; the prose securely supports the structural match but exact algebra needs scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Observed zeta-prime radial analogue matches the CUE distribution shape
accepted_units.why_material: Approximately one hundred thousand derivative zeros in a stated height interval give an empirical distribution with the same striking overall shape as derivative roots of unitary characteristic polynomials.
accepted_units.context_note: The evidence concerns shape in a finite sampled window and does not establish the asymptotic law or explain bimodality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The sample description is textual; the distribution itself is graphical and requires the original figure for quantitative use.

accepted_units.title: One-level density for a unitary ensemble with endpoint multiplicities
accepted_units.why_material: The lemma gives the limiting rescaled one-level density for a circular ensemble weighted by fixed powers at plus and minus one, identifies its Bessel form, and notes the local density near plus one is independent of the opposite-end multiplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: For the paper's collision calculation the relevant specialization is the weight created by two coincident eigenvalues at one.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The measure and Bessel formula are display-dependent; exact exponents and indices should be verified against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Gaudin-Mehta and Szego reduce the conditioned density to local OPUC asymptotics
accepted_units.why_material: The weighted eigenvalue process becomes determinantal through the orthogonal-polynomial projection kernel, so its one-level measure is the kernel diagonal and its microscopic limit reduces to orthogonal-polynomial asymptotics near the conditioned point.
accepted_units.context_note: The dual-polynomial and Szego kernel identities are the bridge from the ensemble measure to an asymptotic analysis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-layer dependent but semantically recoverable; exact conjugations and kernel normalization need preservation.

accepted_units.title: Jacobi asymptotics produce the microscopic Bessel kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Explicit OPUC-to-Jacobi formulas plus microscopic rescaling and Jacobi-to-Bessel asymptotics yield the limiting kernel, its diagonal one-level density, and access to higher correlations and spacings.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivation is summarized as tedious; the unit records the representation chain and resulting kernel rather than filling in omitted algebra.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependence across equations (7.9)-(7.18); exact constants, Bessel indices, and removable phase require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A close pair has a unique analytic derivative root in its diameter disk
accepted_units.why_material: The appendix states a uniform theorem that turns the informal close-pair picture into a unique local derivative root with analytic dependence throughout a truncated configuration domain.
accepted_units.context_note: The threshold is uniform over configurations only for gap height bounded strictly below one over pi and sufficiently large degree.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proposition is clear in prose; the configuration-domain inequalities and disk endpoints are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Argument principle turns root uniqueness into stability of a winding number
accepted_units.why_material: The proof deforms the close-pair disk around possible boundary multiplicities, decomposes the logarithmic derivative into a dominant pair term and a background term, and reduces uniqueness to preserving index one under perturbation.
accepted_units.context_note: No zeros or poles lie on the chosen contour; this is what permits the argument-principle count.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour geometry and logarithmic-derivative displays are readable, though the original figure is useful for orientation.

accepted_units.title: Half-plane localization controls the background logarithmic derivative
accepted_units.why_material: The model image curve has index one, while boundary-arc localization, a sharp real-part maximization, and elementary trigonometric remainder bounds keep the perturbed image in the required half-planes uniformly for gaps below one over pi.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof's positivity margin tends to one minus pi times the gap parameter; that strict margin explains the threshold and the sufficiently-large-degree condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The geometric reasoning is clear, but several interval and inequality displays are fragmented, especially lines 1249-1262; exact constants should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Contour-integral selection certifies analytic dependence of the local root
accepted_units.why_material: Once uniqueness is established, a contour integral represents the selected derivative root and proves analytic dependence locally on compact subsets, hence throughout the configuration-domain interior.
accepted_units.context_note: The contour may be chosen uniformly only on a desired compact subset; the proof then patches these local choices.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the contour-integral display (8.19), which is legible enough for semantics but should be checked for exact numerator and normalization.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Mean-spacing normalization transports a derivative-zero law between two geometries
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Matching local mean spacing converts horizontal displacement from the critical line and radial displacement from the unit circle into parallel scaled variables, after which the close-pair logarithmic-derivative equations have the same leading form.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The zeta side depends on CUE statistics and asymptotic approximations; agreement is solver-independent mathematical evidence only for the model correspondence, not for RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Small-gap statistics become a derivative-root density through an analytic local map
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A close root pair creates a unique nearby derivative root whose even analytic displacement starts quadratically in the gap, so pushing the repulsive small-gap spacing density through this map produces a square-root near-boundary density.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This accounts for the leading close-pair contribution only and relies on ensemble information for background-root coefficients.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The leading close-pair law coexists with non-gap mechanisms and unexplained bimodality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Close pairs dominate the smallest-distance asymptotic without exhausting all near-boundary derivative roots; lower-order separated-root contributions and a robust second mode show that the global distribution needs additional mechanisms.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The second mode is empirical and unexplained, and the cited separated-root examples are described rather than constructed in this source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Collision conditioning links characteristic-polynomial moments to a hard-edge density
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Conditioning two eigenvalues to collide reweights the remaining CUE ensemble by the fourth power of the characteristic polynomial, enabling both ratio-average coefficient calculations and an orthogonal-polynomial derivation of the local Bessel one-level density.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source imports the ratio theorem and Jacobi identities and omits substantial algebra; exact computational reproduction needs those external formulas and scan-verified displays.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Argument-principle rigidity licenses the formal close-pair expansion
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The close-pair logarithmic derivative has a dominant winding-one component; uniform control of the background preserves a unique local root, and contour selection makes that root analytic, justifying its even power-series expansion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Uniformity requires gap height strictly below one over pi and sufficiently large degree; it does not establish a global matching of every gap to a derivative root.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Derivative-zero proximity is a graded diagnostic rather than a direct RH proof route
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Speiser supplies an exact exclusion criterion, while Levinson-style losses and Soundararajan frequency functions turn finer right-of-line proximity into quantitative diagnostics that the CUE calculation can model.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The frequency conjectures and zeta/CUE match remain conditional or conjectural, and none of the source's distributional calculations proves the exclusion required by RH.
